intro.title: Memory Leak Hunt
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that simulates a common source of memory leaks: an event listener that is not properly cleaned up. You will learn the core concept of the useEffect cleanup function, which is essential for preventing memory leaks by removing side effects when a component unmounts. The main technologies involved are React's useState and useEffect hooks, written in TypeScript. By the end, you will understand how to identify potential memory leaks and apply the correct cleanup pattern in your components.
intro.usecase: Memory leaks commonly occur in React applications when components don't properly clean up subscriptions, event listeners, or asynchronous operations. In real-world products like data dashboards with live-updating charts, users switching between different views can leave orphaned WebSocket connections or interval timers running. E-commerce sites with complex product filters and modals often accumulate event listeners that aren't removed when components unmount. Social media feeds with infinite scrolling can leak memory from abandoned API requests and cached data when users navigate away. Proper cleanup prevents gradual performance degradation and crashes in long-running applications.
